subject: Packaging options, safe fallback paths, and stepdown plan for OliveHealth pilot
messages:
From: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@olivehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging for pilot + path to Dedicated; budget constraints

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product overview earlier — Alex and I walked through the hosted demo and liked the latency profile. We're leaning toward a small dedicated pilot for our clinical summarization workflow, but need clarity on packaging and how we can safely move between tiers. Two main questions:

1) If we start on a compact/dedicated pilot (low throughput) what are the defined upgrade and downgrade paths? We need a stepdown we can fall back to if CPU/GPU utilization is below threshold after month 2.

2) What discounting/pricing levers apply for: 6-month pilot, 12-month commit, and a possible 24-month enterprise commit? Our procurement target for unit economics is pretty tight — we have an internal ceiling for first-year spend.

Can you send a concise matrix showing: pilot -> Dedicated 1 (small) -> Dedicated 2 (standard) and the costs, any required seat commitments, and what happens to feature bundles (e.g., KV cache, priority routing, extended retention) when we move between tiers? Also highlight any fallback guarantees (credits, prorations).

We'd like to start the pilot in the first half of September. If you can get a proposal and a rough discount band by EOD Wednesday that helps us prepare the internal business case.

Thanks,

— Procurement Team
OliveHealth
procurement@olivehealth.com


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@olivehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging for pilot + path to Dedicated; budget constraints

Hi — really excited about the pilot timing. Attached is a short proposal and a pricing model that maps the step paths you requested. Key highlights up front:

- Pilot configuration: 2-week ramp, then a 60-day evaluation window on a small Dedicated pool (2 GPUs effective)
- Upgrade path: Pilot -> Dedicated-Compact -> Dedicated-Standard (no migration downtime; model pins preserved).
- Downgrade / safe-fallback: If average sustained utilization < 30% over the 30-day post-pilot window, we offer a one-time prorated credit equal to unused committed capacity and a free 30-day Compact retention extension.

Discount bands (guidance):
- 6-month pilot (no commit): no term discount, but $Xk pilot credit available for onboarding support
- 12-month commit: ~12–15% off list for a minimum monthly committed capacity (we typically seed a ‘pilot-to-commit’ clause that converts pilot usage into billing credits)
- 24-month commit: 18–22% (includes priority capacity and a predictable stepdown SLA)

Feature bundling notes: Certain features (priority routing, extended audit log retention, and custom KV cache allocations) are tied to commit tiers. When you downgrade, those features can be retained for a soft-fallback fee for up to 90 days to prevent sudden behavior regressions.

I've attached: olivehealth_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal + mutual action plan) and olive_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (line-item pricing matrix and stepdown examples).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review proposal and highlight any hard constraints on spend/term.
2) We can schedule a 30-min call Wednesday afternoon to review numbers and finalize discount bounds.
3) If acceptable, we’ll send a DocuSign bundle with a pilot SOW and a conditional conversion clause.

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/preview/OLV-2027-PILOT (final link attached after alignment)

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: olivehealth_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal), olive_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (pricing matrix)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Packaging for pilot + path to Dedicated; budget constraints

Ben / Priyom — forwarding OliveHealth's ask and my initial proposal. Quick context: prospect wants pilot in Sept, tight first-year budget. I'm proposing a 12-month commit band at 12–15% or 24-month at 18–22% with fallback credits for low utilization.

Questions for approvals:
- Can we approve 15% as the high-water for a 12-month commit tied to min monthly committed capacity? If not, is 12% floor acceptable?
- For 24-month, would 18% be the standard pre-approved concession? Also proposing we offer a one-time $10k onboarding credit for the 6-week ramp (helps close pilot).

If we go with 15% we should lock in:
- Conditional conversion clause that makes pilot consumed credits apply to the first billing period if they convert within 30 days after pilot.
- A 90-day soft-fallback fee schedule so we can preserve bundle features if they step down.

Ben — what's the margin impact on a 15% / 12mo commit for a small-dedicated pool? Priyom — any constraints on feature gating (priority routing, retention) when we attach these to commits?

—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: OliveHealth Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@olivehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging for pilot + path to Dedicated; budget constraints

Hi — thanks for the clear asks earlier. Quick update after internal alignment: we can offer the following, subject to final SOW language: 

Final commercial summary (revise as needed):
- Pilot: 60-day small Dedicated pilot (2-GPU equivalent). Onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to first invoice.
- 12-month commit: 12% discount off list for committed baseline usage (with conditional conversion of pilot credits). Includes standard feature bundle (priority routing, 30-day extended audit logs).
- 24-month commit: 18% discount and priority capacity guarantee + 90 days of soft-fallback retention for bundled features.

Safe-fallback and stepdown: if average sustained utilization < 30% for 30 days post-pilot, we will provide a prorated credit for unused committed capacity and preserve feature bundles for up to 90 days under a soft-fallback fee schedule (detailed in attached pricing model).

I've attached the revised proposal and the pricing matrix for your procurement review. If this aligns, I'll send a DocuSign with the pilot SOW + conditional conversion clause and we can lock in September start dates.

DocuSign preview (final after your sign-off): https://app.docusign.com/OLV-2027-PILOT

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
